insights.insight: SINGLE-NAME CONCENTRATION RULE: Never recommend more than one trade in the same sector or with >0.6 correlation. The worst trials (138, 161, 162) all involved correlated double-bets. If two semis score well, take only the highest-conviction one.

When stress >18 AND appetite <35, it MUST generate at least one short/defensive candidate. The current no-trade default on actionable days is the #1 performance leak.

If the last 3-4 days show consistent directional moves (e.g., 4 consecutive down days in Trial 167), override range-bound with directional-trending-down/up. Range-bound should only apply when there are genuine alternating up/down days with no trend.

insights.insight: SEMICONDUCTOR SECTOR PENALTY: Apply a -5 point penalty to all semi trades (LRCX, AMAT, SMH, NVDA, AMD) unless there is a company-specific catalyst (earnings, product launch, export ruling). Generic 'semi rotation' trades have a near-zero win rate in the sample.

insights.insight: BRIEFING-RECOMMENDATION ALIGNMENT CHECK: Add a hard rule that the briefing sentiment and trade direction must agree. Trial 162 briefing was bearish with short recs (aligned), but Trial 161 briefing was bullish with long recs that lost. The issue in 161 was that 'rotation' regime + bullish briefing + semi longs = contradictory signals. If regime says rotation and briefing says bullish, go long in the sector rotating INTO, not the one showing momentum.

insights.insight: Enforce maximum 1 trade per day — the algorithm's only consistent edge is concentrated single-name bets. When multiple candidates pass threshold, take only the highest-scoring one. Multi-trade days have 0% win rate in the sample.

Currently the algorithm goes silent when regime confidence is low, but some of the best individual stock setups occur precisely in uncertain macro environments.

insights.insight: Add a correlation filter: if recommending multiple trades, reject any pair with trailing 20-day correlation above 0.70. Trials 138 (MSFT+AMD), 161 (LRCX+SMH), and 162 (AMAT+SMH) all failed with highly correlated pairs that doubled down on the same directional bet.

Add explicit guardrail: rotation regime → only allow trades in the sector showing relative inflow, not the sector showing outflow.

The current pipeline silently drops opportunities.

insights.insight: REDUCE TIMINGURGENCY WEIGHT AND REBALANCE TOWARD MARKETALIGNMENT: TimingUrgency at 20% is encouraging urgency-driven trades that aren't better than average. MarketAlignment at only 10% is underweighting the single most important regime-alignment factor. The best trades historically (IWM long in risk-on, TGT short during rotation) all had perfect market alignment. Raise marketAlignment to 15% and drop timingUrgency to 10%.

Trial 161 went long in a rotation regime and Trial 162 went short in a rotation regime — rotation should require stronger idiosyncratic catalysts to override the ambiguous directional signal.

insights.insight: LOWER THRESHOLD + ADD REGIME-CONDITIONAL SCORING: Drop the composite threshold from ~70 to 58 to address the 83.5% no-trade rate, BUT add regime-conditional multipliers. Risk-on regimes with >55% confidence get a 1.15x multiplier on long candidates. Range-bound regimes with <40% confidence get a 0.85x penalty on all directional bets. This lets more trades through in high-confidence regimes while staying cautious in ambiguous ones.

insights.insight: TIMING URGENCY AS A GATE, NOT JUST A WEIGHT: Given timingUrgency has the highest predictive power (72.5), use it as a binary pre-filter. If timingUrgency < 60 for a given candidate, disqualify it regardless of composite score. This dimension captures whether there's a time-sensitive reason to act TODAY vs. waiting, and it's the strongest signal of same-day alpha.
